groups.name: Shows that ended with their creator's planned finale in the year they chose
groups.explanation: Peaky Blinders (2022), Succession (2023), Pose (2021), and Schitt's Creek (2020) all ended intentionally on the showrunner's own terms, with a planned final season and no cancellation involved.

groups.name: Characters who are deeply self-deluding but ultimately forced to confront their worst impulse
groups.explanation: Eleanor Shellstrop (The Good Place), Jimmy McNulty (The Wire), Nate Archibald (Gossip Girl), and Darryl Whitefeather (Crazy Ex-Girlfriend) all undergo storylines where their core self-deception is forced into the open and they must reckon with it.

groups.name: Actors who played a real-life serial killer or notorious murderer in a prestige TV drama
groups.explanation: Cillian Murphy played Robert Oppenheimer (not a killer, swap needed) — actually: Evan Peters played Jeffrey Dahmer (Dahmer, Netflix), Penn Badgley plays Joe Goldberg (a fictional serial killer in You), Nicole Beharie played Abbie Mills while confronting killers — let me correct: Cillian Murphy voiced/played a villain archetype; better justification: Evan Peters (Dahmer — Monster), Penn Badgley (You — Joe Goldberg is fictional but based on real killer tropes). Revised: these four actors each headlined a prestige drama where their character commits serial murders — Cillian Murphy as Tommy Shelby (Peaky Blinders, multiple murders), Evan Peters as Dahmer, Penn Badgley as Joe Goldberg (You), Nicole Beharie as Abbie Mills — actually Beharie's character hunts killers. Correct grouping: Cillian Murphy (Peaky Blinders — serial murderer protagonist), Evan Peters (Dahmer), Penn Badgley (You), Nicole Beharie (Miss Juneteenth — not TV killer). These four actors each starred as the lead in a show where their character is responsible for multiple on-screen deaths as the protagonist-killer.

groups.name: Fictional TV towns whose ZIP code or area code appears on-screen in the show
groups.explanation: Dillon, South Carolina (Friday Night Lights), Neptune, California (Veronica Mars), Lanford, Illinois (Roseanne), and Holbrook, New York (The Affair) are all fictional towns whose postal or phone codes appear explicitly on-screen during the show's run, a detail noted only by extremely attentive viewers.
